# lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_cursor.html)- cursor
- [MDB_env](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_env.html)
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_envinfo.html)- envinfo
- Information about the environment
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_stat.html)- stat
- Statistics for a database in the environment
- [MDB_txn](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_txn.html)
- [MDB_val](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_val.html)
- Generic structure used for passing keys and data in and out of the database.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [mdb_cmp](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cmp.html)- ⚠
- Compare two data items according to a particular database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_close.html)- cursor_ - close - ⚠
- Close a cursor handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_count.html)- cursor_ - count - ⚠
- Return count of duplicates for current key.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_dbi.html)- cursor_ - dbi - ⚠
- Return the cursor’s database handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_del.html)- cursor_ - del - ⚠
- Delete current key/data pair
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_get.html)- cursor_ - get - ⚠
- Retrieve by cursor.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_open.html)- cursor_ - open - ⚠
- Create a cursor handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_put.html)- cursor_ - put - ⚠
- Store by cursor.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_renew.html)- cursor_ - renew - ⚠
- Renew a cursor handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_txn.html)- cursor_ - txn - ⚠
- Return the cursor’s transaction handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_close.html)- dbi_ - close - ⚠
- Close a database handle. Normally unnecessary. Use with care:
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_flags.html)- dbi_ - flags - ⚠
- Retrieve the DB flags for a database handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_open.html)- dbi_ - open - ⚠
- Open a database in the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dcmp.html)- dcmp - ⚠
- Compare two data items according to a particular database.
- [mdb_del](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_del.html)- ⚠
- Delete items from a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_drop.html)- drop - ⚠
- Empty or delete+close a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_close.html)- env_ - close - ⚠
- Close the environment and release the memory map.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copy.html)- env_ - copy - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified path.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copy2.html)- env_ - copy2 - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified path, with options.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copyfd.html)- env_ - copyfd - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified file descriptor.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copyfd2.html)- env_ - copyfd2 - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified file descriptor, with options.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_create.html)- env_ - create - ⚠
- Create an LMDB environment handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_fd.html)- env_ - get_ - fd - ⚠
- Return the filedescriptor for the given environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_flags.html)- env_ - get_ - flags - ⚠
- Get environment flags.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_maxkeysize.html)- env_ - get_ - maxkeysize - ⚠
- Get the maximum size of keys and #MDB_DUPSORT data we can write.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_maxreaders.html)- env_ - get_ - maxreaders - ⚠
- Get the maximum number of threads/reader slots for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_path.html)- env_ - get_ - path - ⚠
- Return the path that was used in #mdb_env_open().
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_userctx.html)- env_ - get_ - userctx - ⚠
- Get the application information associated with the #MDB_env.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_info.html)- env_ - info - ⚠
- Return information about the LMDB environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_open.html)- env_ - open - ⚠
- Open an environment handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_assert.html)- env_ - set_ - assert - ⚠
- Set or reset the assert() callback of the environment. Disabled if liblmdb is built with NDEBUG.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_flags.html)- env_ - set_ - flags - ⚠
- Set environment flags.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_mapsize.html)- env_ - set_ - mapsize - ⚠
- Set the size of the memory map to use for this environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_maxdbs.html)- env_ - set_ - maxdbs - ⚠
- Set the maximum number of named databases for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_maxreaders.html)- env_ - set_ - maxreaders - ⚠
- Set the maximum number of threads/reader slots for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_userctx.html)- env_ - set_ - userctx - ⚠
- Set application information associated with the #MDB_env.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_stat.html)- env_ - stat - ⚠
- Return statistics about the LMDB environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_sync.html)- env_ - sync - ⚠
- Flush the data buffers to disk.
- [mdb_get](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_get.html)- ⚠
- Get items from a database.
- [mdb_put](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_put.html)- ⚠
- Store items into a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_reader_check.html)- reader_ - check - ⚠
- Check for stale entries in the reader lock table.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_reader_list.html)- reader_ - list - ⚠
- Dump the entries in the reader lock table.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_compare.html)- set_ - compare - ⚠
- Set a custom key comparison function for a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_dupsort.html)- set_ - dupsort - ⚠
- Set a custom data comparison function for a #MDB_DUPSORT database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_relctx.html)- set_ - relctx - ⚠
- Set a context pointer for a #MDB_FIXEDMAP database’s relocation function.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_relfunc.html)- set_ - relfunc - ⚠
- Set a relocation function for a #MDB_FIXEDMAP database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_stat.html)- stat - ⚠
- Retrieve statistics for a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_strerror.html)- strerror - ⚠
- Return a string describing a given error code.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_abort.html)- txn_ - abort - ⚠
- Abandon all the operations of the transaction instead of saving them.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_begin.html)- txn_ - begin - ⚠
- Create a transaction for use with the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_commit.html)- txn_ - commit - ⚠
- Commit all the operations of a transaction into the database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_env.html)- txn_ - env - ⚠
- Returns the transaction’s #MDB_env
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_id.html)- txn_ - id - ⚠
- Return the transaction’s ID.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_renew.html)- txn_ - renew - ⚠
- Renew a read-only transaction.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_reset.html)- txn_ - reset - ⚠
- Reset a read-only transaction.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_version.html)- version - ⚠
- Return the LMDB library version information.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_assert_func.html)- assert_ - func
- A callback function for most LMDB assert() failures, called before printing the message and aborting.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cmp_func.html)- cmp_ - func
- A callback function used to compare two keys in a database
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cursor_op.html)- cursor_ - op
- Cursor Get operations.
- [MDB_dbi](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_dbi.html)
- A handle for an individual database in the DB environment.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_msg_func.html)- msg_ - func
- A callback function used to print a message from the library.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_rel_func.html)- rel_ - func
- A callback function used to relocate a position-dependent data item in a fixed-address database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_filehandle_t.html)- filehandle_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_mode_t.html)- mode_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_size_t.html)- size_ - t
- Unsigned type used for mapsize, entry counts and page/transaction IDs.

- < Position at previous page and return up to a page of duplicate data items. Only for #MDB_DUPFIXED
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_PREV_NODUP.html)- PREV_ - NODUP
- < Position at last data item of previous key
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_PROBLEM.html)- PROBLEM
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_RDONLY.html)- RDONLY
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_READERS_FULL.html)- READERS_ - FULL
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_RESERVE.html)- RESERVE
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_REVERSEDUP.html)- REVERSEDUP
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_REVERSEKEY.html)- REVERSEKEY
- [MDB_SET](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_SET.html)
- < Position at specified key
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_SET_KEY.html)- SET_ - KEY
- < Position at specified key, return key + data
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/constant.MDB_SET_RANGE.html)- SET_ - RANGE
- < Position at first key greater than or equal to specified key.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [mdb_cmp](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cmp.html)- ⚠
- Compare two data items according to a particular database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_close.html)- cursor_ - close - ⚠
- Close a cursor handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_count.html)- cursor_ - count - ⚠
- Return count of duplicates for current key.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_dbi.html)- cursor_ - dbi - ⚠
- Return the cursor’s database handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_del.html)- cursor_ - del - ⚠
- Delete current key/data pair
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_get.html)- cursor_ - get - ⚠
- Retrieve by cursor.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_open.html)- cursor_ - open - ⚠
- Create a cursor handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_put.html)- cursor_ - put - ⚠
- Store by cursor.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_renew.html)- cursor_ - renew - ⚠
- Renew a cursor handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cursor_txn.html)- cursor_ - txn - ⚠
- Return the cursor’s transaction handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_close.html)- dbi_ - close - ⚠
- Close a database handle. Normally unnecessary. Use with care:
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_flags.html)- dbi_ - flags - ⚠
- Retrieve the DB flags for a database handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_open.html)- dbi_ - open - ⚠
- Open a database in the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dcmp.html)- dcmp - ⚠
- Compare two data items according to a particular database.
- [mdb_del](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_del.html)- ⚠
- Delete items from a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_drop.html)- drop - ⚠
- Empty or delete+close a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_close.html)- env_ - close - ⚠
- Close the environment and release the memory map.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copy.html)- env_ - copy - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified path.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copy2.html)- env_ - copy2 - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified path, with options.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copyfd.html)- env_ - copyfd - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified file descriptor.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copyfd2.html)- env_ - copyfd2 - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified file descriptor, with options.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_create.html)- env_ - create - ⚠
- Create an LMDB environment handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_fd.html)- env_ - get_ - fd - ⚠
- Return the filedescriptor for the given environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_flags.html)- env_ - get_ - flags - ⚠
- Get environment flags.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_maxkeysize.html)- env_ - get_ - maxkeysize - ⚠
- Get the maximum size of keys and #MDB_DUPSORT data we can write.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_maxreaders.html)- env_ - get_ - maxreaders - ⚠
- Get the maximum number of threads/reader slots for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_path.html)- env_ - get_ - path - ⚠
- Return the path that was used in #mdb_env_open().
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_userctx.html)- env_ - get_ - userctx - ⚠
- Get the application information associated with the #MDB_env.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_info.html)- env_ - info - ⚠
- Return information about the LMDB environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_open.html)- env_ - open - ⚠
- Open an environment handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_assert.html)- env_ - set_ - assert - ⚠
- Set or reset the assert() callback of the environment. Disabled if liblmdb is built with NDEBUG.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_flags.html)- env_ - set_ - flags - ⚠
- Set environment flags.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_mapsize.html)- env_ - set_ - mapsize - ⚠
- Set the size of the memory map to use for this environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_maxdbs.html)- env_ - set_ - maxdbs - ⚠
- Set the maximum number of named databases for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_maxreaders.html)- env_ - set_ - maxreaders - ⚠
- Set the maximum number of threads/reader slots for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_userctx.html)- env_ - set_ - userctx - ⚠
- Set application information associated with the #MDB_env.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_stat.html)- env_ - stat - ⚠
- Return statistics about the LMDB environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_sync.html)- env_ - sync - ⚠
- Flush the data buffers to disk.
- [mdb_get](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_get.html)- ⚠
- Get items from a database.
- [mdb_put](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_put.html)- ⚠
- Store items into a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_reader_check.html)- reader_ - check - ⚠
- Check for stale entries in the reader lock table.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_reader_list.html)- reader_ - list - ⚠
- Dump the entries in the reader lock table.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_compare.html)- set_ - compare - ⚠
- Set a custom key comparison function for a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_dupsort.html)- set_ - dupsort - ⚠
- Set a custom data comparison function for a #MDB_DUPSORT database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_relctx.html)- set_ - relctx - ⚠
- Set a context pointer for a #MDB_FIXEDMAP database’s relocation function.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_relfunc.html)- set_ - relfunc - ⚠
- Set a relocation function for a #MDB_FIXEDMAP database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_stat.html)- stat - ⚠
- Retrieve statistics for a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_strerror.html)- strerror - ⚠
- Return a string describing a given error code.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_abort.html)- txn_ - abort - ⚠
- Abandon all the operations of the transaction instead of saving them.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_begin.html)- txn_ - begin - ⚠
- Create a transaction for use with the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_commit.html)- txn_ - commit - ⚠
- Commit all the operations of a transaction into the database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_env.html)- txn_ - env - ⚠
- Returns the transaction’s #MDB_env
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_id.html)- txn_ - id - ⚠
- Return the transaction’s ID.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_renew.html)- txn_ - renew - ⚠
- Renew a read-only transaction.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_reset.html)- txn_ - reset - ⚠
- Reset a read-only transaction.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_version.html)- version - ⚠
- Return the LMDB library version information.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_assert_func.html)- assert_ - func
- A callback function for most LMDB assert() failures, called before printing the message and aborting.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cmp_func.html)- cmp_ - func
- A callback function used to compare two keys in a database
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cursor_op.html)- cursor_ - op
- Cursor Get operations.
- [MDB_dbi](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_dbi.html)
- A handle for an individual database in the DB environment.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_msg_func.html)- msg_ - func
- A callback function used to print a message from the library.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_rel_func.html)- rel_ - func
- A callback function used to relocate a position-dependent data item in a fixed-address database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_filehandle_t.html)- filehandle_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_mode_t.html)- mode_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_size_t.html)- size_ - t
- Unsigned type used for mapsize, entry counts and page/transaction IDs.

- The 64-bit libc on Solaris and illumos only has readdir_r. If a 32-bit Solaris or illumos target is ever created, it should use __posix_readdir_r. See libc(3LIB) on Solaris or illumos: https://illumos.org/man/3lib/libc https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E36784_01/html/E36873/libc-3lib.html https://www.unix.com/man-page/opensolaris/3LIB/libc/

# cstr - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cstr/^0.2.12/

## Expand description

**This crate has been deprecated.
Rust 1.77.0 stabilized  C-string literals.
From that version,  c"abc" can be used in place of cstr!("abc") provided by this crate.
This new feature gives more concise code and faster compilation.
Hence, this crate will no longer be maintained.**

A macro for getting `&'static CStr` from literal or identifier.

This macro checks whether the given literal is valid for `CStr`
at compile time, and returns a static reference of `CStr`.

This macro can be used to initialize constants.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use cstr::cstr;
use std::ffi::CStr;
let test = cstr!(b"hello\xff");
assert_eq!(test, CStr::from_bytes_with_nul(b"hello\xff\0").unwrap());
let test = cstr!("hello");
assert_eq!(test, CStr::from_bytes_with_nul(b"hello\0").unwrap());
let test = cstr!(hello);
assert_eq!(test, CStr::from_bytes_with_nul(b"hello\0").unwrap());
```

# bindgen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bindgen/^0.71.1/

## Expand description

Generate Rust bindings for C and C++ libraries.

Provide a C/C++ header file, receive Rust FFI code to call into C/C++ functions and use types defined in the header.

See the [ Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html) struct for usage.

See the [Users Guide](https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/) for
additional documentation.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [callbacks](https://docs.rs/callbacks/index.html)
- A public API for more fine-grained customization of bindgen behavior.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bindings](https://docs.rs/struct.Bindings.html)
- Generated Rust bindings.
- [Builder](https://docs.rs/struct.Builder.html)
- Configure and generate Rust bindings for a C/C++ header.
- [Cargo](https://docs.rs/struct.CargoCallbacks.html)- Callbacks
- A `ParseCallbacks`implementation that will act on file includes by echoing a rerun-if-changed line and on env variable usage by echoing a rerun-if-env-changed line
- [Clang](https://docs.rs/struct.ClangVersion.html)- Version
- Extracted Clang version data
- [Codegen](https://docs.rs/struct.CodegenConfig.html)- Config
- A type used to indicate which kind of items we have to generate.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/struct.RustTarget.html)- Target
- Represents the version of the Rust language to target.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/enum.Abi.html)
- A valid rust ABI.
- [Alias](https://docs.rs/enum.AliasVariation.html)- Variation
- Enum for how aliases should be translated.
- [Bindgen](https://docs.rs/enum.BindgenError.html)- Error
- Error type for rust-bindgen.
- [Enum](https://docs.rs/enum.EnumVariation.html)- Variation
- A helper type that represents different enum variations.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/enum.FieldVisibilityKind.html)- Visibility - Kind
- What kind of visibility modifier should be used for a struct or field?
- [Formatter](https://docs.rs/enum.Formatter.html)
- Formatting tools that can be used to format the bindings
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/enum.MacroTypeVariation.html)- Type - Variation
- Enum for the default type of macro constants.
- [NonCopy](https://docs.rs/enum.NonCopyUnionStyle.html)- Union - Style
- Enum for how non-`Copy``union`s should be translated.
- [Rust](https://docs.rs/enum.RustEdition.html)- Edition
- Represents Rust Edition for the generated bindings

# cc - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cc/^1.2.37/

## Expand description

A library for [Cargo build scripts](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html)
to compile a set of C/C++/assembly/CUDA files into a static archive for Cargo
to link into the crate being built. This crate does not compile code itself;
it calls out to the default compiler for the platform. This crate will
automatically detect situations such as cross compilation and
[various environment variables](https://docs.rs#external-configuration-via-environment-variables) and will build code appropriately.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

First, you’ll want to both add a build script for your crate (`build.rs`) and
also add this crate to your `Cargo.toml` via:

```
[build-dependencies]
cc = "1.0"
```
Next up, you’ll want to write a build script like so:

```
// build.rs
cc::Build::new()
    .file("foo.c")
    .file("bar.c")
    .compile("foo");
```
And that’s it! Running `cargo build` should take care of the rest and your Rust
application will now have the C files `foo.c` and `bar.c` compiled into a file
named `libfoo.a`. If the C files contain

`void foo_function(void) { ... }`and

`int32_t bar_function(int32_t x) { ... }`you can call them from Rust by declaring them in your Rust code like so:

```
extern "C" {
    fn foo_function();
    fn bar_function(x: i32) -> i32;
}
pub fn call() {
    unsafe {
        foo_function();
        bar_function(42);
    }
}
fn main() {
    call();
}
```
See [the Rustonomicon](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/ffi.html) for more details.

[§](https://docs.rs#external-configuration-via-environment-variables)External configuration via environment variables

To control the programs and flags used for building, the builder can set a number of different environment variables.

- `CFLAGS`- a series of space separated flags passed to compilers. Note that individual flags cannot currently contain spaces, so doing something like:- `-L=foo\ bar`is not possible.
- `CC`- the actual C compiler used. Note that this supports passing a known wrapper via- `sccache cc`. This compiler must understand the- `-c`flag. For certain- `TARGET`s, it also is assumed to know about other flags (most common is- `-fPIC`). ccache, distcc, sccache, icecc, cachepot and buildcache are supported, for sccache, simply set- `CC`to- `sccache cc`. For other custom- `CC`wrapper, just set- `CC_KNOWN_WRAPPER_CUSTOM`to the custom wrapper used in- `CC`.
- `AR`- the- `ar`(archiver) executable to use to build the static library.
- `CRATE_CC_NO_DEFAULTS`- the default compiler flags may cause conflicts in some cross compiling scenarios. Setting this variable will disable the generation of default compiler flags.
- `CC_ENABLE_DEBUG_OUTPUT`- if set, compiler command invocations and exit codes will be logged to stdout. This is useful for debugging build script issues, but can be overly verbose for normal use.
- `CC_SHELL_ESCAPED_FLAGS`- if set,- `*FLAGS`will be parsed as if they were shell arguments (similar to- `make`and- `cmake`) rather than splitting them on each space. For example, with- `CFLAGS='a "b c"'`, the compiler will be invoked with 2 arguments -- `a`and- `b c`- rather than 3:- `a`,- `"b`and- `c"`.
- `CXX...`- see- [C++ Support](https://docs.rs#c-support).
- `CC_FORCE_DISABLE`- If set,- `cc`will never run any- `Command`- `Error`- `Tool`- `Build::get_compiler`- `cc`runs commands in order to locate compilers. Additionally, this does nothing to prevent users from running- `Tool::to_command`- `Command`
- `RUSTC_WRAPPER`- If set, the specified command will be prefixed to the compiler command. This is useful for projects that want to use- [sccache](https://github.com/mozilla/sccache),- [buildcache](https://gitlab.com/bits-n-bites/buildcache), or- [cachepot](https://github.com/paritytech/cachepot).

Furthermore, projects using this crate may specify custom environment variables
to be inspected, for example via the `Build::try_flags_from_environment`
function. Consult the project’s own documentation or its use of the `cc` crate
for any additional variables it may use.

Each of these variables can also be supplied with certain prefixes and suffixes, in the following prioritized order:

- `<var>_<target>`- for example,- `CC_x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`or- `CC_thumbv8m.main-none-eabi`
- `<var>_<target_with_underscores>`- for example,- `CC_x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu`or- `CC_thumbv8m_main_none_eabi`(both periods and underscores are replaced)
- `<build-kind>_<var>`- for example,- `HOST_CC`or- `TARGET_CFLAGS`
- `<var>`- a plain- `CC`,- `AR`as above.

If none of these variables exist, cc-rs uses built-in defaults.

In addition to the above optional environment variables, `cc-rs` has some
functions with hard requirements on some variables supplied by [cargo’s
build-script driver](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#inputs-to-the-build-script) that it has the `TARGET`, `OUT_DIR`, `OPT_LEVEL`,
and `HOST` variables.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

[§](https://docs.rs#parallel)Parallel

Currently cc-rs supports parallel compilation (think `make -jN`) but this
feature is turned off by default. To enable cc-rs to compile C/C++ in parallel,
you can change your dependency to:

```
[build-dependencies]
cc = { version = "1.0", features = ["parallel"] }
```
By default cc-rs will limit parallelism to `$NUM_JOBS`, or if not present it
will limit it to the number of cpus on the machine. If you are using cargo,
use `-jN` option of `build`, `test` and `run` commands as `$NUM_JOBS`
is supplied by cargo.

[§](https://docs.rs#compile-time-requirements)Compile-time Requirements

To work properly this crate needs access to a C compiler when the build script is being run. This crate does not ship a C compiler with it. The compiler required varies per platform, but there are three broad categories:

- Unix platforms require `cc`to be the C compiler. This can be found by installing cc/clang on Linux distributions and Xcode on macOS, for example.
- Windows platforms targeting MSVC (e.g. your target name ends in `-msvc`) require Visual Studio to be installed.`cc-rs`attempts to locate it, and if it fails,`cl.exe`is expected to be available in`PATH`. This can be set up by running the appropriate developer tools shell.- When using `prefer_clang_cl_over_msvc`, make sure that the`C++ Clang compiler for Windows`component is installed through the Visual Studio Installer, so that`cc-rs`can find`clang-cl.exe`.

- When using
- Windows platforms targeting MinGW (e.g. your target name ends in `-gnu`) require`cc`to be available in`PATH`. We recommend the[MinGW-w64](https://www.mingw-w64.org/)distribution. You may also acquire it via[MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org/), as explained[here](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/INSTALL.md#building-on-windows). Make sure to install the appropriate architecture corresponding to your installation of rustc. GCC from older[MinGW](http://www.mingw.org/)project is compatible only with 32-bit rust compiler.

[§](https://docs.rs#c-support)C++ support

`cc-rs` supports C++ libraries compilation by using the `cpp` method on
`Build`:

```
cc::Build::new()
    .cpp(true) // Switch to C++ library compilation.
    .file("foo.cpp")
    .compile("foo");
```
For C++ libraries, the `CXX` and `CXXFLAGS` environment variables are used instead of `CC` and `CFLAGS`.

The C++ standard library may be linked to the crate target. By default it’s `libc++` for macOS, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD, `libc++_shared` for Android, nothing for MSVC, and `libstdc++` for anything else. It can be changed in one of two ways:

- by using the `cpp_link_stdlib`method on`Build`:

```
cc::Build::new()
    .cpp(true)
    .file("foo.cpp")
    .cpp_link_stdlib("stdc++") // use libstdc++
    .compile("foo");
```
- by setting the `CXXSTDLIB`environment variable.

In particular, for Android you may want to [use  c++_static if you have at most one shared library](https://developer.android.com/ndk/guides/cpp-support).

Remember that C++ does name mangling so `extern "C"` might be required to enable Rust linker to find your functions.

[§](https://docs.rs#cuda-c-support)CUDA C++ support

`cc-rs` also supports compiling CUDA C++ libraries by using the `cuda` method
on `Build`:

```
cc::Build::new()
    // Switch to CUDA C++ library compilation using NVCC.
    .cuda(true)
    .cudart("static")
    // Generate code for Maxwell (GTX 970, 980, 980 Ti, Titan X).
    .flag("-gencode").flag("arch=compute_52,code=sm_52")
    // Generate code for Maxwell (Jetson TX1).
    .flag("-gencode").flag("arch=compute_53,code=sm_53")
    // Generate code for Pascal (GTX 1070, 1080, 1080 Ti, Titan Xp).
    .flag("-gencode").flag("arch=compute_61,code=sm_61")
    // Generate code for Pascal (Tesla P100).
    .flag("-gencode").flag("arch=compute_60,code=sm_60")
    // Generate code for Pascal (Jetson TX2).
    .flag("-gencode").flag("arch=compute_62,code=sm_62")
    // Generate code in parallel
    .flag("-t0")
    .file("bar.cu")
    .compile("bar");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#speed-up-compilation-with-sccache)Speed up compilation with sccache

`cc-rs` does not handle incremental compilation like `make` or `ninja`. It
always compiles the all sources, no matter if they have changed or not.
This would be time-consuming in large projects. To save compilation time,
you can use [sccache](https://github.com/mozilla/sccache) by setting
environment variable `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, which will use cached `.o`
files if the sources are unchanged.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [windows_](https://docs.rs/windows_registry/index.html)- registry
- A helper module to looking for windows-specific tools:

# doxygen_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/doxygen-rs/^0.4.2/

## Expand description

Simple Doxygen to Rustdoc translation.

Provides a simple and straightforward API to translate *raw* Doxygen comments to Rustdoc
comments. Purely experimental right now, maybe practical in a future?

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use doxygen_rs::transform;
let rustdoc = transform("@brief Example Doxygen brief");
assert_eq!(rustdoc, "Example Doxygen brief");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#usage-with-bindgen--063)Usage with bindgen >= 0.63

```
#[derive(Debug)]
struct Cb;
impl ParseCallbacks for Cb {
    fn process_comment(&self, comment: &str) -> Option<String> {
        Some(doxygen_rs::transform(comment))
    }
}
```
## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [transform](https://docs.rs/fn.transform.html)
- This function transforms the Doxygen of a single element (function, struct, etc.)

# About Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/about

Docs.rs is an
            [open source](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs)
            documentation host for crates of the
            [Rust Programming Language](https://www.rust-lang.org/).
            All libraries published to [crates.io](https://crates.io)
            are documented. If you just published a crate, your crate is likely
            still in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

            The source code of Docs.rs is available on
            [GitHub](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs). If
            you ever encounter an issue, don't hesitate to report it! (And
            thanks in advance!)

Currently running Docs.rs version is: **0.0.0 (964c90a45859fd8f9076e3cbe58470a5a4f4d4f7 2026-07-01 )**

Summaries of the documentation build processes [are available at /releases/](https://docs.rs/releases).

            JavaScript in support of documentation is allowed but not guaranteed to work on docs.rs. What that
            means: If you write documentation that inlines some JavaScript (like
            [KaTeX](https://katex.org/)), that's allowed, and
            will probably work today but may break in the future.

However, it's not allowed to put JavaScript or other content in docs published on docs.rs for the purpose of tracking visitors. For instance, adding Google Analytics scripts, tracking pixels, or site verification for services like Google Search Console. Crates that do this will have the relevant versions removed and may be blocked from docs.rs.

            Docs.rs is run and maintained by the [Docs.rs team](https://www.rust-lang.org/governance/teams/dev-tools#team-docs-rs).
            You can find us in #t-docs-rs on [Zulip](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/stream/356853-t-docs-rs).

---

# Badges

Source: https://docs.rs/about/badges

Docs.rs no longer has its own badges. Consider using [shields.io](https://shields.io) instead.

# Builds

Source: https://docs.rs/about/builds

Docs.rs automatically builds documentation for crates released on [crates.io](https://crates.io/).
                It may take a while to build your crate, depending on how many crates are in [the queue](https://docs.rs/releases/queue).

                All crates are built in a sandbox using the nightly release of the Rust compiler.
                The current version in use is `rustc 1.98.0-nightly (c397dae80 2026-07-02)`.

                The README displayed on docs.rs follows Cargo’s `package.readme` rules.
                If `readme` is not set, docs.rs will look for `README.md`, `README.txt`, or `README` in the crate root.
                Set `readme = "path/to/file"` to use a custom file, `readme = true` to use `README.md`, or `readme = false` to disable the README.

                To recognize Docs.rs from your Rust code, you can test for the `docsrs` cfg, e.g.:

```
```
                To recognize Docs.rs from `build.rs` files, you can test for the environment variable `DOCS_RS`, e.g.:

`if var.is_ok `
              All targets other than `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` are cross-compiled. For implementation reasons, this is unlikely to change for the foreseeable future.

                You can configure how your crate is built by adding [package metadata](https://docs.rs/metadata) to your `Cargo.toml`, e.g.:

```
[]
 = ["--cfg", "my_cfg"]
```
`#[cfg(my_cfg)]` (not to be confused with `#[cfg(doc)]`) can be used for conditional compilation.
                This approach is also useful for setting
                When you start using docs.rs metadata or `#[cfg(docsrs)]` in your code, you might run into issues
                where your code builds fine locally but fails on docs.rs.
                To avoid this, you can add [ cargo docs-rs](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-docs-rs) to
                your test-suite.
                While it doesn't perfectly replicate our build environment, it can catch many common issues.

                The Docs.rs [README](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/blob/master/README.md#build-subcommand) describes how to build
                unpublished crate documentation locally using the same build environment as the Docs.rs build agent.

                Missing dependencies are a common reason for failed builds.
                Docs.rs dependencies are managed through
                [crates-build-env](https://github.com/rust-lang/crates-build-env).
                See [Forge](https://forge.rust-lang.org/docs-rs/add-dependencies.html) for how to add a dependency.

                Most of the sandbox is a read-only file system, including the source directory of your crate and its dependencies.
                If your `build.rs` generates files that are relevant for documentation, consider writing to the
                [cargo output directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/environment-variables.html#environment-variables-cargo-sets-for-crates),
                passed in the environment variable `OUT_DIR`.

All the builds are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The current limits are:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                If your build fails because it hit one of these limits, please
                [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                to get them increased for your crate.
                Since our build agent has finite resources, we have to consider each case individually. However, there are a few general policies:

If your crate fails to build for a reason not listed here, you can rebuild it from [crates.io](https://crates.io) website as you can see below:

Or you can [file an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues) if you think it's a **docs.rs** issue.

# Metadata

Source: https://docs.rs/about/metadata

You can customize docs.rs builds by defining `[package.metadata.docs.rs]`
		table in your crates' `Cargo.toml`.

The available configuration flags you can customize are:

```
[]
 = "test"
[]
# Features to pass to Cargo (default: [])
 = ["feature1", "feature2"]
# Whether to pass `--all-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Whether to pass `--no-default-features` to Cargo (default: false)
 = true
# Target to test build on, used as the default landing page (default: "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu")
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
 = "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"
# Targets to build (default: see below)
#
# Any target supported by rustup can be used.
#
# Default targets:
# - x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - aarch64-apple-darwin
# - x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
# - aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
# - i686-pc-windows-msvc
#
# Set this to `[]` to only build the default target.
#
# If `default-target` is unset, the first element of `targets` is treated as the default target.
# Otherwise, these `targets` are built in addition to the default target.
# If both `default-target` and `targets` are unset,
#   all tier-one targets will be built and `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` will be used as the default target.
 = ["aarch64-apple-darwin", "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"]
# If you want to instead add another target without overwriting the default ones:
 = ["i686-apple-darwin"]
# Additional `RUSTFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustc-arg"]
# Additional `RUSTDOCFLAGS` to set (default: [])
 = ["--example-rustdoc-arg"]
# List of command line arguments for `cargo`.
#
# These cannot be a subcommand, they may only be options.
 = ["-Z", "build-std"]
```

# Shorthand URLs

Source: https://docs.rs/about/redirections

Docs.rs uses semver to parse URLs. You can use this feature to access
            crates' documentation easily. Example of URL redirections for
            `clap` crate:

| URL | Redirects to documentation of |
|---|---|
| [docs.rs/clap](https://docs.rs/clap) | Latest version of clap |
| [docs.rs/clap::Command](https://docs.rs/clap::Command) | Latest version of clap, and search for "Command" within the crate |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2) | 2.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/~2.9](https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2.9) | 2.9.* version |
| [docs.rs/clap/2.9.3](https://docs.rs/clap/2.9.3) | 2.9.3 version (you don't need `=`unlike semver) |
| [docs.rs/clap/*](https://docs.rs/clap/*) | Latest version of this page (if it still exists). "latest" or "newest" work as well as `*`. |

---

# Download

Source: https://docs.rs/about/download

docs.rs stores the `rustdoc` output in a ZIP file.

                These archives can be used as a base for further processing of
                the documentation for offline readers like Dash or Zeal.
                **They are not directly usable for offline documentation.**

The download is possible for specific or semantic versions:

But also viaTo unpack the ZIP file you need any zip utility that supports PKZIP version 4.6 and BZIP2 & Deflate compression.

The archives will contain all the documentation HTML files for all targets and CSS/JS assets that are specific to the build. The default target will be found at the root, and other targets each in its own subfolder.

                Docs.rs is running rustdoc with `--static-root-path "/-/rustdoc.static/"`,
                which leads to all references to static assets breaking if they are not
                available under that path. Older builds used `--static-root-path "/"`, which
                means you will have to handle both.

                Since we're also adding `--emit=invocation-specific` to our build
                the archives will *not* contain any static assets that are specific to the
                toolchain. For now these will have to be downloaded file-by-file directly
                from docs.rs.

---

# Rustdoc JSON

Source: https://docs.rs/about/rustdoc-json

docs.rs builds & hosts the [ rustdoc JSON](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/unstable-features.html#json-output) output.

This structured version of the documentation can be used for inspecting the docs and types of the crate in a programmatic way.

                The JSON file you're downloading might have been built with an older version of `rustdoc`
                so you might have to check the `format_version` attribute to determine how to parse the structure.
                The [ rustdoc-types](https://docs.rs/rustdoc-types/) crate helps with this.

**
                We started building rustdoc JSON on 2025-05-23. So any release before that won't have a download
                available until our rebuilds reached that release.
            **

                The download URLs can be generic or specific, depending on what you need. In case of rebuilds we
                also keep old format versions around. **Until we rebuilt all releases, we might return
                a `404 NOT FOUND` for some.**

By default we use `zstd` compression, which is more space efficient and faster to decompress. For more limited environments we also started supporting `gzip` compression. You can receive gzip by adding `.gz` to the given URL.

Here some URL examples you can use.

| URL | Redirects to JSON download of |
|---|---|
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json) | latest version, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json.gz) | latest version, default target, latest format-version, gzip compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/json/42) | latest version, default target, format-version 42 |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/~4/json.zst](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/%7E4/json.zst) | latest v4 via semver, default target, latest format-version, zstd compression |
| [https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json](https://docs.rs/crate/clap/latest/i686-pc-windows-msvc/json) | latest version, windows target, latest format-version |

# sim_lib_music_transform - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sim-lib-music-transform/0.1.0-rc.1/sim_lib_music_transform/

## Expand description

Music transformation layer for the SIM music constellation.

This crate applies transformations to musical material: classic operations
such as transpose, invert, retrograde, augment, and diminish; configurable
pitch and time remaps; pattern mutators; and a capability-gated custom event
filter pipeline. Transforms read a `MusicObject` into a canonical
`PianoRoll` and return new `Music`, optionally paired with diagnostics in a
[ TransformReport](https://docs.rs/struct.TransformReport.html).

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Callable](https://docs.rs/struct.CallableFilterDefinition.html)- Filter - Definition
- A named, reusable filter definition stored in a registry.
- [Callable](https://docs.rs/struct.CallableFilterRef.html)- Filter - Ref
- A by-name reference to a registered callable filter.
- [Callable](https://docs.rs/struct.CallableFilterRegistry.html)- Filter - Registry
- Lookup table of `CallableFilterDefinition`
- [Callable](https://docs.rs/struct.CallablePitchMap.html)- Pitch - Map
- Named pitch map that applies a fixed chromatic offset to each pitch.
- [Custom](https://docs.rs/struct.CustomFilter.html)- Filter
- A declared, capability-gated event filter with input/output shapes.
- [Custom](https://docs.rs/struct.CustomFilterRun.html)- Filter - Run
- Output of evaluating a custom filter: produced events and traces.
- [Custom](https://docs.rs/struct.CustomFilterTrace.html)- Filter - Trace
- A single recorded step of a custom filter’s evaluation.
- [Custom](https://docs.rs/struct.CustomPitchAxis.html)- Pitch - Axis
- Named inversion axis carrying an explicit pitch.
- [Filter](https://docs.rs/struct.FilterCapabilitySet.html)- Capability - Set
- An ordered set of `FilterCapability`
- [Filter](https://docs.rs/struct.FilterContext.html)- Context
- Runtime grants and seed supplied when evaluating a custom filter.
- [Filter](https://docs.rs/struct.FilterRule.html)- Rule
- A `when -> op`rule: an operation applied to matching events.
- [Filter](https://docs.rs/struct.FilterShape.html)- Shape
- The set of lane kinds a filter port accepts.
- [Function](https://docs.rs/struct.FunctionMapRegistry.html)- MapRegistry
- Lookup table of `FunctionMap`
- [IntMatrix](https://docs.rs/struct.IntMatrix.html)
- Integer 2x3 affine matrix mapping `(degree, octave, 1)`to a new pitch.
- [Invert](https://docs.rs/struct.InvertTransform.html)- Transform
- Inversion transform that mirrors pitch about a `PitchAxis`
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternLockSet.html)- Lock - Set
- Set of source note indices held fixed (locked) during mutation.
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternMutatorConfig.html)- Mutator - Config
- Configuration describing a sequence of pattern mutations and their controls.
- [Pattern](https://docs.rs/struct.PatternMutatorPlayer.html)- Mutator - Player
- Player that applies a `PatternMutatorConfig`
- [Retrograde](https://docs.rs/struct.RetrogradeTransform.html)- Transform
- Retrograde transform that reverses material under a `RetrogradeMode`
- [Time](https://docs.rs/struct.TimeMapPoint.html)- MapPoint
- One `(input -> output)`breakpoint in a piecewise-linear time map.
- [Transform](https://docs.rs/struct.TransformChain.html)- Chain
- An ordered pipeline of `TransformStep`
- [Transform](https://docs.rs/struct.TransformDiagnostic.html)- Diagnostic
- A single diagnostic emitted by a transform, tagged with its origin.
- [Transform](https://docs.rs/struct.TransformReport.html)- Report
- Result of a transform: the produced music plus any diagnostics raised.
- [Transpose](https://docs.rs/struct.TransposeTransform.html)- Transform
- Transpose transform that shifts pitch by a `PitchDelta`
- [Tuning](https://docs.rs/struct.TuningRemap.html)- Remap
- Microtonal tuning offset expressed in cents.
- [Warp](https://docs.rs/struct.WarpMarker.html)- Marker
- A warp anchor pairing a source time with its target time.

- [Pitch](https://docs.rs/enum.PitchRemap.html)- Remap
- A pitch remapping strategy applied note by note across material.
- [Retrograde](https://docs.rs/enum.RetrogradeMode.html)- Mode
- Strategy for placing notes when reversing material in time.
- [Stretch](https://docs.rs/enum.StretchPolicy.html)- Policy
- Strategy for stretching or warping material along the time axis.
- [Transform](https://docs.rs/enum.TransformDiagnosticCode.html)- Diagnostic - Code
- Classification of a problem a transform encountered while running.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [augment](https://docs.rs/fn.augment.html)
- Lengthens every onset and duration by `factor`(time augmentation).
- [chord_](https://docs.rs/fn.chord_tones_in.html)- tones_ - in
- Snaps every note to the nearest pitch belonging to the given scale.
- [diminish](https://docs.rs/fn.diminish.html)
- Shortens every onset and duration by `factor`(time diminution).
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_custom_filter_codec.html)- custom_ - filter_ - codec
- Checks that a codec name is supported by the custom filter surface.
- [lane_](https://docs.rs/fn.lane_kind_from_wire.html)- kind_ - from_ - wire
- Parses a lane kind from its wire label, if recognized.
- [loop_n](https://docs.rs/fn.loop_n.html)
- Repeats the material `n`times back to back along the time axis.
- [map_](https://docs.rs/fn.map_to_function.html)- to_ - function
- Remaps each in-key note to the same scale degree under another function.
- [mutate_](https://docs.rs/fn.mutate_pattern.html)- pattern
- Applies a `PatternMutatorConfig`
- [pitch_](https://docs.rs/fn.pitch_class_name.html)- class_ - name
- Returns the canonical name of a pitch class.
- [pitch_](https://docs.rs/fn.pitch_invert.html)- invert
- Inverts every note’s pitch about the given axis pitch.
- [player_](https://docs.rs/fn.player_mutator.html)- mutator
- Builds a `PatternMutatorPlayer`
- [quarter](https://docs.rs/fn.quarter.html)
- Returns the `Time`value for one quarter note (1/4).
- [retrograde](https://docs.rs/fn.retrograde.html)
- Reverses the material in time using the default `RetrogradeMode::Cutout`
- [retrograde_](https://docs.rs/fn.retrograde_invert.html)- invert
- Applies `pitch_invert``retrograde`
- [retrograde_](https://docs.rs/fn.retrograde_with_mode.html)- with_ - mode
- Reverses the material in time using the given `RetrogradeMode`
- [shift_](https://docs.rs/fn.shift_octave.html)- octave
- Shifts every note by the given number of whole octaves.
- [silence](https://docs.rs/fn.silence.html)
- Builds a `Rest`spanning the given duration.
- [simple_](https://docs.rs/fn.simple_melody.html)- melody
- Builds a single-voice `Melody`from`(MIDI key, duration)`pairs.
- [slice](https://docs.rs/fn.slice.html)
- Extracts the `[start, end)`time window, clipping note spans to the bounds.
- [time_](https://docs.rs/fn.time_invert.html)- invert
- Mirrors note onsets about the total duration, then rebases to start at zero.
- [transpose](https://docs.rs/fn.transpose.html)
- Transposes every note chromatically by the given number of semitones.
- [transpose_](https://docs.rs/fn.transpose_diatonic.html)- diatonic
- Transposes every note by `steps`scale degrees within the given scale.

# lash_s3_store - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lash-s3-store/0.1.0-alpha.82/lash_s3_store/

## Expand description

S3-compatible attachment storage for Lash.

This crate stores attachment bytes in any S3-compatible object store,
including AWS S3 and MinIO. Runtime metadata and attachment manifests remain
in the configured [ lash_core::RuntimePersistence](https://docs.rs/lash-core/0.1.0-alpha.82/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lash_core/store/trait.RuntimePersistence.html) backend.

# lash_lashlang_runtime - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lash-lashlang-runtime/0.1.0-alpha.82/lash_lashlang_runtime/

A per-link record of every deferred resolution, keyed by call-path within
the execution scope. Replay/recovery applies the record so the resolver is
never called twice for the same link. Captures both Resolved grants (with
their Tool Execution Binding) and negative NotAvailable results.

A host-authorized tool capability resolved for a deferred call-path. It
carries the callable contract and Lashlang identity (via the tool
definition) plus the host-owned Tool Execution Binding that routes a call to
the backing account, service, secret, or remote executor.

Marker key that wraps a Type literal at its outermost level so a host-side
consumer can tell a Type value apart from a plain record. The inner value
is the JSON-Schema representation of the type.

Map the lashlang language crate’s durability tier onto the runtime’s
lash_core::DurabilityTier. The two enums are parallel; this is the single
bridge point between them (the parallel LashlangDurabilityTier alias is
gone — process engines self-describe their tier via lash_core::DurabilityTier).

gather → resolve → link: resolve_and_fold_deferred then link. Used by
callers that do not maintain their own compile cache. NotAvailable (and no
resolver) leaves the symbol unresolved, surfacing a clean model-visible link
error.

gather → resolve: collect every module call-path program references,
resolve the ones host_environment does not already provide (without
failing fast on the first), record the outcomes, and fold Resolved grants
into host_environment. Returns the augmented host environment; the caller
links (or compiles via a cache) against it.

---

- [llm](https://docs.rs/llm/index.html)
- LLM request/response envelopes: messages, attachments, tool specs, output specs, provider metadata, and schema-projection contracts.
- [observations](https://docs.rs/observations/index.html)
- Session observation: cursors, resumable observation events, and live replay gap envelopes.
- [processes](https://docs.rs/processes/index.html)
- Process lifecycle envelopes: start/cancel/signal/await/list requests and results, process records and summaries, event semantics, execution environments, and runtime invocation provenance.
- [prompt](https://docs.rs/prompt/index.html)
- Prompt-layer envelopes: templates, slots, and contributions.
- [registry_](https://docs.rs/registry_errors/index.html)- errors
- The protocol error type, plus the remote tool-registry contract and its reopen-stability assertion.
- [tools](https://docs.rs/tools/index.html)
- Tool grants: schemas, call-path bindings, activation, scheduling, and retry policies.
- [triggers](https://docs.rs/triggers/index.html)
- Trigger envelopes: occurrence emission, subscriptions, and registrations.
- [turn_](https://docs.rs/turn_input/index.html)- input
- Turn input envelopes: items, image blobs, per-turn protocol options, and the turn request.
- [turn_](https://docs.rs/turn_result/index.html)- result
- Turn result envelopes: the turn result itself, outcomes, stops, assistant output, usage/execution summaries, tool-call summaries, issues, and causal references.
- [usage_](https://docs.rs/usage_activity/index.html)- activity
- Token usage accounting and the streaming turn-activity event vocabulary.

# lash_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lash-core/0.1.0-alpha.82/lash_core/

## Expand description

Runtime kernel for Lash.

The process kernel intentionally understands `ToolCall`, `SessionTurn`, and
`External` because those inputs carry runtime mechanisms core must enforce:
tool orchestration, child-session turns, and externally completed work. New
process runtimes should use `ProcessInput::Engine { kind, payload }` unless
core must understand their semantics to enforce a kernel mechanism.

Protocols follow the same boundary: core owns the `HostTurnProtocol` state
shape and the `ProtocolDriverPlugin` slot, while external protocol crates
provide the driver implementation.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- [append_](https://docs.rs/fn.append_assistant_text_part.html)- assistant_ - text_ - part

- Convert a raw `LlmResponse`into a stream of`LlmOutputPart`s that downstream code can iterate. When the response only carries`full_text`(provider didn’t populate`parts`), synthesize a single`Text`part.

- Build a Reasoning `Part`from a reasoning item.`meta`is Some when the item carries provider replay metadata; None for display-only summaries.
- [render_](https://docs.rs/fn.render_turn_causes_prompt.html)- turn_ - causes_ - prompt
- [resolve_](https://docs.rs/fn.resolve_prompt_layers.html)- prompt_ - layers

- [shared_](https://docs.rs/fn.shared_parts.html)- parts
- Wrap a `Vec<Part>`for the`Message::parts`field. Use this in struct literals and tests (`parts: shared_parts(vec![Part { ... }])`) so the call sites stay short and uniform.
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_tool_input.html)- tool_ - input
- [visible_](https://docs.rs/fn.visible_response_parts.html)- response_ - parts
- Apply provider phase semantics to response parts. If a Responses-family
provider emits both `commentary`and`final_answer`text, the latter is the final assistant prose and commentary is retained only in the raw provider response, not in user-visible prose projection.
- [visible_](https://docs.rs/fn.visible_response_text_from_parts.html)- response_ - text_ - from_ - parts

# lash_rlm_types - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lash-rlm-types/0.1.0-alpha.82/lash_rlm_types/

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [RlmAttachment](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmAttachmentRef.html)- Ref
- [RlmCreate](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmCreateExtras.html)- Extras
- RLM protocol session config. Natural turns finish with prose-only model
responses or explicit `finish <value>`from lashlang. Programmatic turns can require an explicit finish value, optionally validated against a schema.`final_answer_format`is a session presentation preference; schema-required turns ignore it.
- [RlmDiagnostic](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmDiagnosticEvent.html)- Event
- [RlmGlobals](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmGlobalsPatchPluginBody.html)- Patch - Plugin - Body
- [RlmImage](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmImageRef.html)- Ref
- [RlmProjected](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmProjectedSeedSnapshot.html)- Seed - Snapshot
- Wire-format snapshot of a set of projected bindings. Pairs of
`(name, json_value)`that get re-projected as host bindings on the child session at creation time. This is the serializable form of`lash_protocol_rlm::RlmProjectedBindings`; lash-rlm-types stays free of any runtime dependency on lashlang itself.
- [RlmProjection](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmProjection.html)
- [RlmSeed](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmSeedPluginBody.html)- Plugin - Body
- [RlmTrajectory](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmTrajectoryEntry.html)- Entry
- [RlmTurn](https://docs.rs/struct.RlmTurnProtocol.html)- Protocol

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [PROJECTED_](https://docs.rs/constant.PROJECTED_JSON_TAG.html)- JSON_ - TAG
- Reserved JSON key used as the canonical wire encoding for
`lashlang::Value::Projected`across the lashlang→host bridge. When the model passes a projected source as a tool argument, lashlang serializes it as`{"__projected__": <inner>}`.
- [PROJECTION_](https://docs.rs/constant.PROJECTION_REF_JSON_TAG.html)- REF_ - JSON_ - TAG

- [referenced_](https://docs.rs/fn.referenced_module_call_paths.html)- module_ - call_ - paths
- Collect the module call-paths (`module.operation`, dotted for nested modules) that a parsed program references through receiver calls. This is the “gather” step of deferred tool resolution: the host resolver is asked to resolve any returned path that the link-time host environment does not already provide.
- [register_](https://docs.rs/fn.register_call_args.html)- call_ - args
- [static_](https://docs.rs/fn.static_graph_json.html)- graph_ - json
- [trigger_](https://docs.rs/fn.trigger_event_placeholder_expr.html)- event_ - placeholder_ - expr
- [unwrap_](https://docs.rs/fn.unwrap_type_value.html)- type_ - value
- Unwrap a `Value::Record`that carries the`$lash_type`marker back into the inner JSON-Schema value. Returns`None`when the value is not a wrapped Type literal.
- [walk_](https://docs.rs/fn.walk_expr.html)- expr

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_assert_func.html)- assert_ - func
- A callback function for most LMDB assert() failures, called before printing the message and aborting.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cmp_func.html)- cmp_ - func
- A callback function used to compare two keys in a database
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cursor_op.html)- cursor_ - op
- Cursor Get operations.
- [MDB_dbi](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_dbi.html)
- A handle for an individual database in the DB environment.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_msg_func.html)- msg_ - func
- A callback function used to print a message from the library.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_rel_func.html)- rel_ - func
- A callback function used to relocate a position-dependent data item in a fixed-address database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_filehandle_t.html)- filehandle_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_mode_t.html)- mode_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_size_t.html)- size_ - t
- Unsigned type used for mapsize, entry counts and page/transaction IDs.

- [mdb_cmp](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_cmp.html)- ⚠

- Close a database handle. Normally unnecessary. Use with care:
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_flags.html)- dbi_ - flags - ⚠
- Retrieve the DB flags for a database handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dbi_open.html)- dbi_ - open - ⚠
- Open a database in the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_dcmp.html)- dcmp - ⚠
- Compare two data items according to a particular database.
- [mdb_del](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_del.html)- ⚠
- Delete items from a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_drop.html)- drop - ⚠
- Empty or delete+close a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_close.html)- env_ - close - ⚠
- Close the environment and release the memory map.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copy.html)- env_ - copy - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified path.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copy2.html)- env_ - copy2 - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified path, with options.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copyfd.html)- env_ - copyfd - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified file descriptor.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_copyfd2.html)- env_ - copyfd2 - ⚠
- Copy an LMDB environment to the specified file descriptor, with options.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_create.html)- env_ - create - ⚠
- Create an LMDB environment handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_fd.html)- env_ - get_ - fd - ⚠
- Return the filedescriptor for the given environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_flags.html)- env_ - get_ - flags - ⚠
- Get environment flags.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_maxkeysize.html)- env_ - get_ - maxkeysize - ⚠
- Get the maximum size of keys and #MDB_DUPSORT data we can write.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_maxreaders.html)- env_ - get_ - maxreaders - ⚠
- Get the maximum number of threads/reader slots for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_path.html)- env_ - get_ - path - ⚠
- Return the path that was used in #mdb_env_open().
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_get_userctx.html)- env_ - get_ - userctx - ⚠
- Get the application information associated with the #MDB_env.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_info.html)- env_ - info - ⚠
- Return information about the LMDB environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_open.html)- env_ - open - ⚠
- Open an environment handle.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_assert.html)- env_ - set_ - assert - ⚠
- Set or reset the assert() callback of the environment. Disabled if liblmdb is built with NDEBUG.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_flags.html)- env_ - set_ - flags - ⚠
- Set environment flags.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_mapsize.html)- env_ - set_ - mapsize - ⚠
- Set the size of the memory map to use for this environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_maxdbs.html)- env_ - set_ - maxdbs - ⚠
- Set the maximum number of named databases for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_maxreaders.html)- env_ - set_ - maxreaders - ⚠
- Set the maximum number of threads/reader slots for the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_set_userctx.html)- env_ - set_ - userctx - ⚠
- Set application information associated with the #MDB_env.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_stat.html)- env_ - stat - ⚠
- Return statistics about the LMDB environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_env_sync.html)- env_ - sync - ⚠
- Flush the data buffers to disk.
- [mdb_get](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_get.html)- ⚠
- Get items from a database.
- [mdb_put](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_put.html)- ⚠
- Store items into a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_reader_check.html)- reader_ - check - ⚠
- Check for stale entries in the reader lock table.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_reader_list.html)- reader_ - list - ⚠
- Dump the entries in the reader lock table.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_compare.html)- set_ - compare - ⚠
- Set a custom key comparison function for a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_dupsort.html)- set_ - dupsort - ⚠
- Set a custom data comparison function for a #MDB_DUPSORT database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_relctx.html)- set_ - relctx - ⚠
- Set a context pointer for a #MDB_FIXEDMAP database’s relocation function.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_set_relfunc.html)- set_ - relfunc - ⚠
- Set a relocation function for a #MDB_FIXEDMAP database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_stat.html)- stat - ⚠
- Retrieve statistics for a database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_strerror.html)- strerror - ⚠
- Return a string describing a given error code.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_abort.html)- txn_ - abort - ⚠
- Abandon all the operations of the transaction instead of saving them.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_begin.html)- txn_ - begin - ⚠
- Create a transaction for use with the environment.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_commit.html)- txn_ - commit - ⚠
- Commit all the operations of a transaction into the database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_env.html)- txn_ - env - ⚠
- Returns the transaction’s #MDB_env
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_id.html)- txn_ - id - ⚠
- Return the transaction’s ID.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_renew.html)- txn_ - renew - ⚠
- Renew a read-only transaction.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_txn_reset.html)- txn_ - reset - ⚠
- Reset a read-only transaction.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/fn.mdb_version.html)- version - ⚠
- Return the LMDB library version information.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_assert_func.html)- assert_ - func
- A callback function for most LMDB assert() failures, called before printing the message and aborting.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cmp_func.html)- cmp_ - func
- A callback function used to compare two keys in a database
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_cursor_op.html)- cursor_ - op
- Cursor Get operations.
- [MDB_dbi](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_dbi.html)
- A handle for an individual database in the DB environment.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_msg_func.html)- msg_ - func
- A callback function used to print a message from the library.
- [MDB_](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_rel_func.html)- rel_ - func
- A callback function used to relocate a position-dependent data item in a fixed-address database.
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_filehandle_t.html)- filehandle_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_mode_t.html)- mode_ - t
- [mdb_](https://docs.rs/type.mdb_size_t.html)- size_ - t
- Unsigned type used for mapsize, entry counts and page/transaction IDs.

# MDB_val in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/struct.MDB_val.html

## Expand description

Generic structure used for passing keys and data in and out of the database.

Values returned from the database are valid only until a subsequent update operation, or the end of the transaction. Do not modify or free them, they commonly point into the database itself.

Key sizes must be between 1 and #mdb_env_get_maxkeysize() inclusive. The same applies to data sizes in databases with the #MDB_DUPSORT flag. Other data items can in theory be from 0 to 0xffffffff bytes long.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.mv_size)

`mv_size: `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)< size of the data item

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.mv_data)

`mv_data: `[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[c_void](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ffi/enum.c_void.html)< address of the data item

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# mdb_cmp in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/fn.mdb_cmp.html

```
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mdb_cmp(
    txn:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_txn](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_txn.html),
    dbi: [MDB_dbi](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_dbi.html),
    a: [*const ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_val](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_val.html),
    b: [*const ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_val](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_val.html),
) -> [c_int](https://docs.rs/libc/0.2.175/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libc/primitives/type.c_int.html)## Expand description

Compare two data items according to a particular database.

This returns a comparison as if the two data items were keys in the specified database.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `txn`(direction in) - A transaction handle returned by #mdb_txn_begin()
- `dbi`(direction in) - A database handle returned by #mdb_dbi_open()
- `a`(direction in) - The first item to compare
- `b`(direction in) - The second item to compare

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

< 0 if a < b, 0 if a == b, > 0 if a > b

# mdb_cursor_close in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

# mdb_cursor_del in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/fn.mdb_cursor_del.html

```
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mdb_cursor_del(
    cursor:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_cursor.html),
    flags: [c_uint](https://docs.rs/libc/0.2.175/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libc/primitives/type.c_uint.html),
) -> [c_int](https://docs.rs/libc/0.2.175/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libc/primitives/type.c_int.html)## Expand description

Delete current key/data pair

This function deletes the key/data pair to which the cursor refers. This does not invalidate the cursor, so operations such as MDB_NEXT can still be used on it. Both MDB_NEXT and MDB_GET_CURRENT will return the same record after this operation.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `cursor`(direction in) - A cursor handle returned by #mdb_cursor_open()
- `flags`(direction in) - Options for this operation. This parameter must be set to 0 or one of the values described here.

- #MDB_NODUPDATA - delete all of the data items for the current key. This flag may only be specified if the database was opened with #MDB_DUPSORT.

A non-zero error value on failure and 0 on success. Some possible errors are:

- EACCES - an attempt was made to write in a read-only transaction.
- EINVAL - an invalid parameter was specified.

---

# mdb_cursor_open in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/fn.mdb_cursor_open.html

```
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mdb_cursor_open(
    txn:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_txn](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_txn.html),
    dbi: [MDB_dbi](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_dbi.html),
    cursor: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_cursor](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_cursor.html),
) -> [c_int](https://docs.rs/libc/0.2.175/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libc/primitives/type.c_int.html)## Expand description

Create a cursor handle.

A cursor is associated with a specific transaction and database. A cursor cannot be used when its database handle is closed. Nor when its transaction has ended, except with #mdb_cursor_renew(). It can be discarded with #mdb_cursor_close(). A cursor in a write-transaction can be closed before its transaction ends, and will otherwise be closed when its transaction ends. A cursor in a read-only transaction must be closed explicitly, before or after its transaction ends. It can be reused with #mdb_cursor_renew() before finally closing it.

Note:Earlier documentation said that cursors in every transaction were closed when the transaction committed or aborted.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `txn`(direction in) - A transaction handle returned by #mdb_txn_begin()
- `dbi`(direction in) - A database handle returned by #mdb_dbi_open()
- `cursor`(direction out) - Address where the new #MDB_cursor handle will be stored

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

A non-zero error value on failure and 0 on success. Some possible errors are:

- EINVAL - an invalid parameter was specified.

---

# mdb_dbi_close in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/fn.mdb_dbi_close.html

## Expand description

Close a database handle. Normally unnecessary. Use with care:

This call is not mutex protected. Handles should only be closed by a single thread, and only if no other threads are going to reference the database handle or one of its cursors any further. Do not close a handle if an existing transaction has modified its database. Doing so can cause misbehavior from database corruption to errors like MDB_BAD_VALSIZE (since the DB name is gone).

Closing a database handle is not necessary, but lets #mdb_dbi_open() reuse the handle value. Usually it’s better to set a bigger #mdb_env_set_maxdbs(), unless that value would be large.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `env`(direction in) - An environment handle returned by #mdb_env_create()
- `dbi`(direction in) - A database handle returned by #mdb_dbi_open()

---

# mdb_del in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/fn.mdb_del.html

```
pub unsafe extern "C" fn mdb_del(
    txn:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_txn](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_txn.html),
    dbi: [MDB_dbi](https://docs.rs/type.MDB_dbi.html),
    key: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_val](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_val.html),
    data: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)[MDB_val](https://docs.rs/struct.MDB_val.html),
) -> [c_int](https://docs.rs/libc/0.2.175/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/libc/primitives/type.c_int.html)## Expand description

Delete items from a database.

This function removes key/data pairs from the database. If the database does not support sorted duplicate data items (#MDB_DUPSORT) the data parameter is ignored. If the database supports sorted duplicates and the data parameter is NULL, all of the duplicate data items for the key will be deleted. Otherwise, if the data parameter is non-NULL only the matching data item will be deleted. This function will return #MDB_NOTFOUND if the specified key/data pair is not in the database.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `txn`(direction in) - A transaction handle returned by #mdb_txn_begin()
- `dbi`(direction in) - A database handle returned by #mdb_dbi_open()
- `key`(direction in) - The key to delete from the database
- `data`(direction in) - The data to delete

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

A non-zero error value on failure and 0 on success. Some possible errors are:

- EACCES - an attempt was made to write in a read-only transaction.
- EINVAL - an invalid parameter was specified.

---

# mdb_env_copy in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/fn.mdb_env_copy.html

## Expand description

Copy an LMDB environment to the specified path.

This function may be used to make a backup of an existing environment. No lockfile is created, since it gets recreated at need.

Note:This call can trigger significant file size growth if run in parallel with write transactions, because it employs a read-only transaction. See long-lived transactions under caveats_sec.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `env`(direction in) - An environment handle returned by #mdb_env_create(). It must have already been opened successfully.
- `path`(direction in) - The directory in which the copy will reside. This directory must already exist and be writable but must otherwise be empty.

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

A non-zero error value on failure and 0 on success.

---

# mdb_env_create in lmdb_master_sys - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lmdb-master-sys/0.2.6/lmdb_master_sys/fn.mdb_env_create.html

## Expand description

Create an LMDB environment handle.

This function allocates memory for a #MDB_env structure. To release the allocated memory and discard the handle, call #mdb_env_close(). Before the handle may be used, it must be opened using #mdb_env_open(). Various other options may also need to be set before opening the handle, e.g. #mdb_env_set_mapsize(), #mdb_env_set_maxreaders(), #mdb_env_set_maxdbs(), depending on usage requirements.

[§](https://docs.rs#arguments)Arguments

- `env`(direction out) - The address where the new handle will be stored

[§](https://docs.rs#returns)Returns

A non-zero error value on failure and 0 on success.
